# Release Notes: v1.0.9

> This file is the source of truth for the GitHub Release body.
> The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release-android.yml`)
> copies this file's contents as the Release body via `body_path`.

## Correctness

- **Invalid counts are now rejected, not silently dropped (web)** — caller-supplied
  counts are validated before any write: at most 8 trackers, at most 10 000 per
  tracker, at most 50 entries per write, and keys restricted to
  `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`. Out-of-range input fails fast with `INVALID_COUNT` instead
  of being filtered away and appearing to succeed. Stored and legacy state is still
  *normalised* (filtered) rather than rejected, so existing accounts keep loading
- **Duplicate tracker creation prevented** — creating a tracker is single-flight on
  both clients, so a double tap no longer produces two trackers or two idempotent
  writes
- **Server-authoritative ledger listener gated** — the Option B live ledger
  subscription now starts only when the account's financial mode resolves to the
  trusted-server path, and re-gates when the mode changes, so a `LEGACY` account
  never opens a listener it cannot use

## Security

- **Firebase App Check removed from both clients** — no attestation provider is
  installed, no App Check token is requested, and no enforcement is configured;
  the now-unused App Check hosts are gone from the Hosting CSP. This is a
  deliberate scope decision, documented in `SECURITY.md`, and it does **not**
  weaken owner isolation: every Firestore path still requires
  `request.auth.uid == userId`. Note that API-key restrictions reduce casual reuse
  of the public key but are **not** App Check and **not** a substitute for
  authorization
- **Functions dependency advisory cleared** — `body-parser` 2.3.0 → **2.4.0**
  (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 / CVE-2026-111181, high). The fix is lockfile-only: it
  satisfies Express's existing `^2.3.0` range, so `firebase-functions` and
  `express` are unchanged. `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` now reports
  **0 vulnerabilities**
- **Firestore Security Rules are unchanged** — byte-identical to the previous
  release; no new denial was introduced or removed

## CI

- **Android instrumentation results are now enforced by a fail-closed gate** — the
  previous `grep`/`awk` extraction of JUnit XML has been replaced by a parser that
  rejects a missing results directory, missing or stale XML, malformed XML,
  unexpected structure, inconsistent totals, all-skipped runs, non-numeric or
  negative attributes, and a Gradle exit code that disagrees with the XML. It is
  covered by 26 regression tests that run before the emulator starts
- Instrumentation counts in the workflow comments corrected to the real suite
  size (22 + 9 = 31)

## Maintenance

- Repository audit published under `docs/audit-2026-10-26.md`, together with the
  reconciled hardening notes in `docs/release-hardening/`
- `README.md` gains an **Engineering decisions** section explaining the stack,
  the shared-Kotlin and contract-test strategy, the Spark plan, why App Check is
  absent, and how CI covers all three surfaces
- 10.1 MB of per-theme screenshots referenced by no file were removed; the
  README showcase images are unchanged
- Suites at this release: 584 web unit, 76 contract, 176 Firestore-rules, 62
  Functions unit, 25 Functions emulator integration, 257 Android JVM, and 31
  Android instrumentation tests

## Compatibility

- No Cloud Functions are deployed and no Blaze plan is required; the app runs
  entirely on the Firebase Spark plan (Auth + Firestore + Hosting)
- No change to Authentication configuration, billing, or production data
